summary.en: Israel is positioning forces to resume an offensive in southern Lebanon, contingent on renewed fighting with Iran, while Hezbollah continues artillery fire on Israeli positions and has begun cash payments to war victims and displaced families. The Israeli army has built a new road in the Shebaa Valley buffer zone, expanding its presence near the border. The United Nations reports 300,000 people displaced in Lebanon by the fighting. 4,335 battle-related deaths occurred in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Israel posisjonerer styrker for å gjenoppta et offensiv i sørlige Libanon, avhengig av fornyet kamp med Iran, mens Hizbollah fortsetter artilleriskudd mot israelske posisjoner og har begynt å betale kontantstøtte til krigsofre og fordrevne familier. Den israelske hæren har bygget en ny vei i bufferområdet Shebaa-dalen, og utvider sin tilstedeværelse nær grensen. FN rapporterer at 300 000 personer er fordrevet i Libanon på grunn av kampene. 4 335 dødsfall knyttet til kamp forekom i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Hezbollah–Israel conflict (2023–present)
background.extract: An ongoing conflict between the Lebanese militant group Hezbollah and Israel began on 8 October 2023, when Hezbollah launched rockets and artillery at Israeli positions following Hamas's October 7 attacks on Israel. The conflict escalated into a prolonged exchange of bombardments, leading to extensive displacement in Israel and Lebanon. The conflict is part of the broader Middle Eastern crisis that began with Hamas's attack, with the short Israeli invasion of Lebanon in 2024 marking the largest escalation of the Hezbollah–Israel conflict since the 2006 Lebanon War. In Arabic, the conflict (2023–2024) is referred to as the "Support War" or the "Gaza Support War."
